story.title: Special Representative for Colombia's remarks to the Security Council [as delivered] - DPPA

facts.text: I am pleased that the Security Council is today resuming the good practice of including the voices of civil society in its meetings on Colombia.
When the Council meets next on Colombia in July, elections will have concluded, and a new Government will be preparing to begin its term in August.
Whoever assumes the presidency will face a formidable challenge in consolidating peace and security in the regions still affected by conflict.
The Verification Mission stands ready to continue to assist the Colombians along this path.
Despite the difficulties, it remains a path that is well worth following.
Allow me to reiterate in this regard the Secretary-General's congratulations on the peaceful participation of the Colombian people in the legislative elections held in March.

Despite concerns during the campaign period over incidents of violence and the presence of illegal armed groups in conflict-affected regions, adequate measures were taken and election day was not adversely affected by security incidents — a demonstration of Colombia’s strong institutions.
It is essential for the country to stay on this trajectory.
We have fully restructured the Mission to reflect the refocused mandate and streamlined further in line with UN80 reductions.
Colombia remains today more peaceful than during peak years of the conflict.
Their ongoing clashes over territorial control and illicit economies are bringing violence and hardship to entire communities.
We condemn, among others, their increased recruitment and use of children.
It is an honor to participate alongside Her Excellency Rosa Villavicencio, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Colombia.
She also exemplifies the important role that women have played in building peace in Colombia.
It is my pleasure to brief the Security Council once again on Colombia.
Miroslav Jenča, Special Representative of the Secretary-General and Head of the United Nations Verification Mission in Colombia
The opportunity is there to make use of the instruments of the Agreement and the presence of the Mission across Colombia’s conflict-affected regions to contribute substantially toward these ends.
The Council’s role has been critical in supporting Colombia’s path to peace, and I deeply appreciate its constant support for the Verification Mission.
These are key factors that have fuelled violence for decades in Colombia.
We carry out verification with a proactive spirit of assisting the parties to overcome bottlenecks to moving forward in implementation.
The Mission is also investing in digital innovation aimed at optimizing its analysis and verification in the field.

Colombia has begun a new political chapter with wide ranging challenges ahead and the need for sustained international engagement in order to overcome remaining obstacles, deepen the gains achieved to date and build a more peaceful and secure future for all Colombians.
DPPA is at the heart of United Nations efforts to prevent and resolve conflict, advance diplomacy and mediation, and build sustainable peace around the world.
